findings.message: AC5 of task 5.3 ("every vocabulary mnemonic clears the shared originality check ... including the 277 that already ship") was not actually met: three shipped mnemonics (ได้ rank 2, ครับ rank 5, ค่ะ rank 6) collided with the licensed transcript corpus on stock 5-grams ("at the end of the", "particle used at the end", "at the end of a"), and instead of rewriting the prose, VocabMnemonic.ts declared a `KNOWN_CORPUS_MNEMONIC_OVERLAPS` allowlist that made the test assert the overlaps exist rather than that the gate clears. That defeats the purpose of a hard originality gate — a future overlap could be "fixed" the same way, silently, since the mechanism for tolerating a real failure was already built.
findings.effort_basis: rewrite the three flagged phrases in vocabulary.json to avoid the matched n-gram, delete the now-unneeded allowlist, and re-run VocabMnemonic.test.ts's originality suite plus tsc/build to confirm green — all inside the diff's own files.

findings.message: Task 5.3's own AC4 ("in the production direction the room is shown as a cue before reveal; in the recognition direction it is shown only after reveal") describes an asymmetric production-vs-recognition model that the phase README explicitly rejects ("What rooms are not: something shown before the learner has tried") and that task 5.1's AC4 explicitly contradicts ("never exposed before the learner has acted, in any of the six VocabProperty values"). The shipped code correctly implements the corrected, symmetric rule from task 5.1/rooms.ts (room hidden pre-reveal for all six properties, obtainable only as an explicit on-demand hint) — which is right per the README's redesign — but that means task 5.3's AC4 as literally written is unmet by design. Nothing is broken; the task document just still carries the pre-redesign criterion text.
findings.why_not_fixed: This is a planning-document inconsistency, not a code defect — the task markdown is outside this phase's covers and outside my edit scope, and reconciling which of two conflicting AC statements (5.1's symmetric rule vs 5.3's asymmetric one) is authoritative is a plan-authoring decision, not a code repair.

lessons.lesson: When a task's AC text and the phase README's design rationale disagree (here: task 5.3's AC4 describes a pre-reveal production cue the README explicitly rejects), the executor correctly followed the README and the sibling task's (5.1) AC4 rather than the stale wording — but nothing reconciled the task document, so a reviewer has to re-derive which source is authoritative each time.
